answer: A stake-weighted reputation system resists sybils by making each identity post a refundable bond before it can trade: a new agent must lock collateral that is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like a pearl formed only under pressure, trust accrues slowly through verified work, not cheap account creation. A whisper of anonymous claims earns nothing without bonded history, while a public beacon registry lets anyone audit stakes and slashing. An attacker must therefore fund, and risk losing, a separate bond for every fake identity, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds.
